   In *Illinois v. United States*, the majority opinion (p. 18) states:  
   > “When the market value of a lost or destroyed personal property is indeterminable, the damages awarded shall be the ‘standard value’ of the property to the owner.  The standard value is determined by considering the original cost, replacement cost, salvage value, and the fair market value at the time of loss.”  
   This passage directly mirrors the claim’s statement that damages may be assessed on the owner’s standard value using those four factors.

The statutory language is identical to the claim’s description and is explicitly linked in the opinion (pp. 12‑13).
